source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
3. List the date and time of the inspection. Ensure accuracy as this serves as a reference for when the failed safety checks occurred.

4. Identify the location where the inspection took place by stating the exact address, name of the building, and any specific part or floor that was inspected.

5. Document the name and credentials of the inspecting official or the fire safety officer who conducted the inspection. This person’s signature may also be required at the end of the report.

6. Use a checklist to detail the specific fire safety systems and procedures assessed. Common items include:
   - Fire alarms
   - Smoke detectors
   - Emergency lighting
   - Fire extinguishers
   - Sprinkler systems
   - Fire doors
   - Escape plans and routes
   - Fire drills and employee training
   - Other relevant safety equipment and preventative measures

7. Highlight areas where the inspection has identified failure. Be clear and concise with your descriptions
